explanation: Spot on! Family-centred care treats the baby and the family as one team, making sure you work closely with the loved ones who know the child best. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h1)

question: When a nurse visits a family's home to care for an infant, why is it helpful to view yourself as a 'guest'?

options.A: To respect the family's home environment and autonomy
options.B: To prevent the nurse from providing direct physical care
options.C: Because family members must supervise every nursing task
options.D: Because home nurses have fewer legal responsibilities

explanation: You got it! Walking into someone's home means respecting their private space, culture, and routines. It's the best way to build real trust. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h1)

question: By what age does a typical infant double their birth weight?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Twelve months

explanation: Infants generally double their birth weight by six months of age and triple it by twelve months. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h2)

question: What exciting new skill does an infant show when they develop a pincer grasp?

options.A: Support the entire weight of the body on the legs
options.B: Pick up small objects using the thumb and index finger
options.C: Roll over from the abdomen to the back easily
options.D: Hold a heavy feeding bottle without any assistance

explanation: Exactly! The pincer grasp is a fun milestone where baby uses their thumb and index finger like tiny tweezers to grab small bits of food. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h2)

question: At what age are solid foods typically introduced to an infant's diet?

options.A: Four months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Two months
options.D: Ten months

explanation: World Health Organization and pediatric guidelines recommend exclusive breastfeeding or formula feeding for the first six months, followed by the introduction of complementary solid foods. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h3)

question: A mother asks if she should give her four-month-old plain water on a very hot afternoon. What is the best response?

options.A: Give small amounts of boiled water between feedings
options.B: Replace one milk feeding with water to cool the baby
options.C: Breast milk or formula already provides enough hydration
options.D: Add sugar to the water to prevent low blood sugar

explanation: You nailed it! Babies under six months don't need extra water. Breast milk or formula has all the fluid they need, even when the weather is hot. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h3)

question: Which sleeping position is best recommended to lower the risk of SIDS in infants?

options.A: Upright position in a carrier
options.B: Prone position on the stomach
options.C: Side-lying position with a roll
options.D: Supine position on the back

explanation: Correct! Always remember: 'Back to sleep' is the safest and most effective way to protect infants from SIDS. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why should soft pillows and stuffed animals be kept out of an infant's crib?

options.A: They create a suffocation and entrapment hazard
options.B: They attract household insects near the bedding
options.C: They cause severe skin rashes on the baby's face
options.D: They prevent the infant from sleeping deeply

explanation: Spot on! Soft toys and pillows can easily block a tiny baby's airway, posing a major suffocation risk during sleep. Keep the cot clear! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the best home care approach for managing a mild diaper rash?

options.A: Keeping the skin clean, dry, and applying a barrier ointment
options.B: Covering the rash tightly with plastic-lined pants
options.C: Scrubbing the affected area with perfumed soap daily
options.D: Applying strong prescription steroid creams immediately

explanation: Great choice! Diaper rash clears up fastest when you keep the skin dry, change diapers frequently, and use a soothing barrier cream. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which finding in an infant always requires a prompt medical checkup?

options.A: Sneezing once or twice after exposure to morning sunlight
options.B: Spitting up a small amount of milk after a burping session
options.C: A rectal temperature of 38.0°C or higher in a two-month-old
options.D: Having yellow, soft, seedy stools when being breastfed

explanation: Spot on! Any fever in a baby under three months old is an emergency. Always have it checked right away to rule out serious infections. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of connecting new parents with community support groups?

options.A: Ensuring the nurse no longer needs to visit the home
options.B: Providing free financial assistance for all household expenses
options.C: Reducing feelings of isolation and sharing practical experiences
options.D: Replacing the need for routine pediatric medical checkups

explanation: You got it! Support groups let parents share everyday struggles, find emotional encouragement, and learn great tips from other parents. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical community resource recommended for families with an infant?

options.A: Lactation consultant services
options.B: Early childhood intervention programs
options.C: Adult vocational retraining centers
options.D: Immunization and vaccination clinics

explanation: Correct! Vocational centers are for adult job training. Families with infants need resources focused on child health, feeding, and early development. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is a major advantage of providing home health care to new and expectant mothers?

options.A: It removes all financial costs associated with medical care.
options.B: It ensures the mother will have zero physical complications.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe the home environment and family support.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any future doctor visits.

explanation: Visiting the home gives nurses a clear picture of the patient's living conditions and support system, which directly impacts recovery and health. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is building a trusting relationship especially important during home health visits?

options.A: It guarantees that the infant will sleep through the night.
options.B: It stops family members from asking questions about the treatment.
options.C: It encourages the mother to share open and honest details about her health.
options.D: It legally protects the nursing agency from any liability issues.

explanation: Trust helps patients feel safe, making them more likely to share true symptoms and personal concerns that affect their care. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is the term for the process where the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state after delivery?

options.A: Duplication
options.B: Hypertrophy
options.C: Hemodilution
options.D: Involution

explanation: Involution refers to the rapid process by which the uterus and other body systems return to their non-pregnant size and condition. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why do many pregnant women experience mild shortness of breath during normal daily activities?

options.A: The heart chambers shrink in size to handle less blood flow.
options.B: The growing uterus pushes the diaphragm upward against the lungs.
options.C: Airways narrow due to chronic allergic reactions in pregnancy.
options.D: Red blood cell production suddenly drops to dangerously low levels.

explanation: As the fetus grows, the upward pressure on the diaphragm leaves less room for the lungs to fully expand during deep breaths. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is a primary assessment tool used during a home prenatal visit to check fetal well-being?

options.A: Peak flow meter
options.B: Digital thermometer
options.C: Doppler device
options.D: Glucometer strip

explanation: A portable Doppler is used during home visits to listen to the fetal heart rate and confirm fetal viability. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h3)

question: A pregnant home-care patient has a single high blood pressure reading. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all prescribed prenatal vitamins.
options.B: Immediately discharge the patient from home care services.
options.C: Perform serial blood pressure checks and notify the primary provider.
options.D: Wait until the scheduled monthly clinic visit to mention it.

explanation: A single high reading needs re-checking to confirm a trend, and the provider must be informed promptly to rule out gestational hypertension. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h3)

question: When assessing a postpartum mother at home, what does a firm uterine fundus indicate?

options.A: A delayed healing process of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: An abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity
options.C: Effective muscle contraction to prevent excessive bleeding
options.D: Complete closure of the cervix back to normal size

explanation: A firm uterus compresses open blood vessels at the placental site, which is vital for preventing postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h4)

question: How does a home care nurse primarily evaluate adequate hydration and feeding in a newborn?

options.A: Checking the flexibility of the baby's finger joints
options.B: Weighing the baby before and after every single nursing session
options.C: Counting the number of wet and soiled diapers per day
options.D: Measuring the exact length of the infant every morning

explanation: Tracking wet diapers is a reliable, non-invasive way to ensure the newborn is receiving enough milk and staying hydrated. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of potential postpartum preeclampsia at home?

options.A: Increased appetite and mild weight gain
options.B: Mild swelling in the toes after a long walk
options.C: Occasional dry skin on the hands and arms
options.D: Severe persistent headache and blurred vision

explanation: Severe headaches and vision changes are key neurological symptoms associated with dangerous blood pressure spikes in preeclampsia. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe finding and requires immediate reporting during a postpartum home visit?

options.A: Slight breast tenderness as milk production begins
options.B: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and a low-grade fever
options.C: Normal postpartum fatigue after a night of interrupted sleep
options.D: Mild lochia rubra that gradually decreases over two weeks

explanation: Foul-smelling discharge and fever point toward a uterine infection (endometritis), which requires prompt medical evaluation and antibiotics. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why is adequate daily intake of folate (folic acid) especially important early in pregnancy?

options.A: To help prevent neural tube defects in the developing fetus
options.B: To stop the mother from developing gestational diabetes
options.C: To increase the total volume of red blood cells in the father
options.D: To prevent the baby from being born with weak bones

explanation: Folic acid plays a vital role in early cell division and the proper formation of the brain and spinal cord during early pregnancy. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h6)

question: What nutritional guidance should a home health nurse give to a newly postpartum breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Stop drinking water with meals to prevent overhydration.
options.B: Increase daily calorie and fluid intake to support milk production.
options.C: Avoid all dairy products to improve the baby's digestion.
options.D: Immediately start a strict low-calorie diet to lose pregnancy weight.

explanation: Breastfeeding burns extra calories and requires higher fluid intake to maintain a healthy milk supply and keep the mother energized. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is an important preventive screening topic for women receiving long-term home health care?

options.A: Daily testing for adult growth hormone levels
options.B: Mammogram schedules and breast self-awareness
options.C: Monthly surgical checks for joint replacement
options.D: Weekly testing for acute kidney stone formation

explanation: Regular breast screenings and awareness are key components of preventive health maintenance for adult women. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h7)

question: Why are private discussions during home visits particularly beneficial for women's health assessments?

options.A: They prevent family members from ever asking questions about medications.
options.B: They legally replace the need for any laboratory blood testing.
options.C: They help women feel comfortable discussing sensitive issues like domestic safety.
options.D: They ensure the patient will never experience chronic illness.

explanation: Privacy builds confidence, allowing patients to safely share private health concerns, mental struggles, or safety risks at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h7)

question: What is a key safety step a home health nurse should take with a pregnant patient in case of an emergency?

options.A: Instruct the family to never call emergency services under any condition.
options.B: Encourage the patient to drive herself to the hospital if pain starts.
options.C: Establish a clear emergency plan and post local hospital numbers visibly.
options.D: Leave complex medical equipment in the home without instructions.

explanation: Having a clear, visible emergency plan ensures that family members can act quickly and correctly when urgent signs appear. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h8)

question: A home health nurse notices signs of severe postpartum depression during a visit. What is the best collaborative action?

options.A: Wait until the baby is one year old before mentioning the concern.
options.B: Tell the family that mood changes always resolve completely on their own.
options.C: Refer the mother to a mental health specialist or social worker promptly.
options.D: Prescribe an antidepressant medication during the home visit.

explanation: Involving mental health professionals and social workers ensures the patient receives safe, specialized support for postpartum mood disorders. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h8)

question: What is the main goal of maternal home healthcare visits in our communities?

options.A: To bridge the gap between hospital services and community living
options.B: To distribute free prescription drugs to every household
options.C: To replace the need for hospital delivery entirely
options.D: To enforce strict hospital rules inside family compounds

explanation: Home visits let you bring health education and monitoring right to the doorstep of mothers who find it hard to visit the clinic regularly. You're making healthcare accessible where they live! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is it so important to respect local customs and beliefs when doing home visits?

options.A: Nurses are legally required to practice traditional medicine first
options.B: Traditional beliefs strongly influence local health practices and family acceptance
options.C: Hospitals have no influence over community health traditions
options.D: Foreign donors demand strict adherence to local customs

explanation: When you respect people's traditions, they trust you more. This openness stops families from hiding things from you and helps them accept helpful health advice. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why do we always push iron and folate supplements during antenatal care?

options.A: To cure existing chronic infections in the uterus
options.B: To increase the total body weight of the mother
options.C: To speed up the physical growth of the mother's hair
options.D: To prevent anemia and neural tube defects in the baby

explanation: Iron keeps the mother's blood strong and fights off tiredness (anemia), while folate protects the baby's developing brain and spine. It's a powerful combo! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h2)

question: A pregnant farmer asks you if she should stop all physical work. What is your best advice?

options.A: Continue heavy farming work as normal to build endurance
options.B: Switch entirely to night shifts for all physical activities
options.C: Stop working immediately and stay in bed until delivery
options.D: Avoid exhausting labor and heavy lifting while resting often

explanation: Light activity is totally fine and healthy, but heavy lifting and exhausting work can put stress on the pregnancy. Encourage her to listen to her body and rest well. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which simple, portable tool does a nurse use during a home visit to check the baby's heartbeat?

options.A: An electronic MRI scanner
options.B: A Pinard stethoscope or fetoscope
options.C: A standard household thermometer
options.D: A digital blood pressure cuff

explanation: The Pinard stethoscope is a classic, durable tool that doesn't need batteries—making it super reliable for checking fetal heart tones right in the home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h3)

question: What does severe, lasting swelling in a pregnant woman's lower legs usually tell you?

options.A: Normal muscle growth in the lower extremities
options.B: Potential fluid retention and vascular complications
options.C: A sign of high physical activity and exercise
options.D: Excessive intake of clean drinking water

explanation: A little swelling can happen towards the end of pregnancy, but heavy or persistent swelling (edema) is a red flag to check her blood pressure for pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which of these is a serious danger sign in pregnancy that means 'go to the clinic now'?

options.A: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy
options.B: A slight increase in normal daily appetite
options.C: Mild fatigue after walking short distances
options.D: Mild morning nausea during the first trimester

explanation: Bleeding is never normal when expecting. It's always a warning sign that needs immediate medical evaluation to keep both mother and baby safe. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why must a pregnant woman report blurred vision and a terrible headache immediately?

options.A: They mean the mother needs stronger reading glasses
options.B: They are common signs of normal hormonal adjustment
options.C: They show that the baby is moving too much inside
options.D: They indicate severe high blood pressure or pre-eclampsia

explanation: Headaches and changes in vision are classic warning signs of dangerously high blood pressure. Catching pre-eclampsia early saves lives! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h4)

question: During a postnatal home visit, why do you gently feel (palpate) the mother's lower tummy?

options.A: To align the spine of the postpartum mother
options.B: To check if the uterus is contracting firmly and shrinking
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the mammary glands
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the new baby

explanation: A firm uterus means it's clamping down properly, which stops bleeding from where the placenta was attached. That's a huge relief for postpartum recovery! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which finding in a new mother's lochia (postnatal discharge) should worry you the most?

options.A: A foul or offensive odor coming from the discharge
options.B: A slight increase in flow when the mother stands up
options.C: Small dark clots passed during the first three days
options.D: A gradual fading from red to pink over two weeks

explanation: Lochia naturally changes color and has a normal earthy smell, but a foul odor is a major sign of a uterine infection (endometritis) that needs quick treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h5)

question: What must mothers avoid putting on a newborn baby's umbilical cord stump?

options.A: Clean air and dry gauze
options.B: Traditional concoctions, saliva, or oils
options.C: Recommended antiseptic solutions
options.D: Clean water and mild soap

explanation: Putting unsterile substances like herbs, saliva, or oils on the cord introduces nasty bacteria and tetanus spores. Keep it clean and dry instead! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why is it so important for a baby to latch wide onto the areola during breastfeeding?

options.A: It increases the total daily urine output of the infant
options.B: It prevents the baby from spitting up after meals
options.C: It forces the baby to sleep longer through the night
options.D: It prevents maternal nipple soreness and ensures milk transfer

explanation: A good, wide latch helps the baby get plenty of milk easily while saving the mother from cracked, painful nipples. Technique is everything! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is the main difference between normal 'baby blues' and severe postpartum depression?

options.A: Mild tearfulness and fatigue on the third day after birth
options.B: Temporary excitement followed by a brief afternoon nap
options.C: Persistent sadness and a lack of interest in caring for the baby
options.D: Increased appetite and eagerness to clean the house

explanation: Baby blues pass in a few days, but postpartum depression brings deep, long-lasting sadness and makes it hard for the mother to bond with her baby. She needs support! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h7)

question: A new mother looks exhausted and tells you she feels totally hopeless weeks after delivery. What should you do first?

options.A: Provide a supportive listening ear and involve family in her care
options.B: Tell her to ignore her feelings and focus entirely on chores
options.C: Leave her alone so she can sleep without any interruptions
options.D: Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately to gain rest

explanation: Start by listening without judgment and bringing her support system on board. Validating her feelings is a great first step toward healing. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h7)

question: Why do we encourage families to plan emergency transport before the baby arrives?

options.A: To reduce delays in reaching a health facility during complications
options.B: To replace the need for professional community nurses
options.C: To lower the financial cost of routine antenatal medications
options.D: To train family members to perform emergency surgeries at home

explanation: When an emergency happens, every minute counts. Having transport figured out beforehand prevents fatal delays in getting to the hospital. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h8)

question: Why should community health nurses team up with traditional birth attendants and local leaders?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from rural households
options.B: To stop all traditional practices permanently by force
options.C: To ensure coordinated care and prompt referral of dangerous cases
options.D: To hand over all clinical nursing duties to local leaders

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with local leaders builds strong community trust, ensuring that mothers with complications get rushed to the hospital safely and quickly. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h8)

question: What is a major reason why many women still experience home deliveries in rural Nigeria?

options.A: The complete absence of trained community midwives
options.B: Limited access to formal health facilities
options.C: Strict hospital policies banning pregnant women
options.D: A direct instruction from the federal government

explanation: Many women in rural areas rely on home delivery because distance and transportation challenges prevent them from reaching a hospital in time. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is the primary role of a community nurse during a home birth setting?

options.A: To replace traditional birth attendants without community consent
options.B: To bridge the gap between traditional practices and safe clinical care
options.C: To document births for statistical purposes only
options.D: To force every laboring mother to relocate to a tertiary hospital immediately

explanation: Community nurses work closely within local populations to provide safe, evidence-based care while respecting and understanding local birth choices. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which condition is considered a high-risk factor that rules out a safe home delivery?

options.A: A normal vertex presentation at term
options.B: A history of a previous cesarean section
options.C: A history of a single normal spontaneous vaginal birth
options.D: A maternal age between twenty and thirty

explanation: Previous uterine scars carry a risk of uterine rupture during labor, making hospital delivery mandatory. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: A community nurse is inspecting a pregnant woman's home delivery kit. Which item is UNNECESSARY or unsafe for newborn cord care?

options.A: A clean, sterile razor blade for cutting the cord
options.B: Traditional herbal mixture applied directly to the cut cord
options.C: Clean thread to tie off the umbilical cord securely
options.D: Soap and clean water for thorough handwashing

explanation: Applying unsterile substances like herbal mixtures to the umbilical cord introduces bacteria and causes severe neonatal infections like tetanus. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary medication administered immediately after birth to prevent postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Ferrous sulfate
options.C: Paracetamol
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: Oxytocin causes the uterine muscles to contract firmly, compressing blood vessels at the placental site to stop bleeding. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why is drying the newborn baby immediately after birth a critical nursing action?

options.A: To stimulate the baby to learn how to walk
options.B: To remove the vernix completely so the skin breathes
options.C: To check for hidden birthmarks and bruises
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

explanation: Wet skin combined with room air causes rapid evaporation and heat loss, which can lead to dangerous cold stress in newborns. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h3)

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening complication that can occur during the third stage of labor?

options.A: Neonatal jaundice
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum depression

explanation: Excessive bleeding after delivery can lead to hypovolemic shock and maternal death within a very short time if not managed urgently. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: A woman at home experiences heavy vaginal bleeding shortly after delivering the placenta. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Send a family member to buy oral iron supplements from a local shop
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform immediate uterine massage and administer oxytocin
options.D: Document the estimated blood loss in the register

explanation: Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs stimulate contractions to clamp down open blood vessels and stop the bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding for a healthy newborn?

options.A: Until the first tooth appears
options.B: First two weeks of life
options.C: First six months of life
options.D: First twelve months of life

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding provides all necessary nutrients and antibodies without needing water or other foods for the first six months. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h5)

question: What does a nurse check when assessing normal uterine involution during a postnatal home visit?

options.A: The complete absence of lochia discharge after twenty-four hours
options.B: The permanent softening of the abdominal wall muscles
options.C: The gradual decrease in the size and height of the uterus
options.D: The rapid increase in maternal body weight

explanation: Involution is the normal process where the uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy size, felt as a steadily lowering fundal height. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why is birth spacing emphasized during family planning counseling for postpartum women?

options.A: It allows the mother's body and nutrient stores to recover fully
options.B: It prevents the mother from ever experiencing menopause
options.C: It guarantees that all future children will be born male
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical checkups

explanation: Spacing pregnancies gives the mother adequate time to restore her health and nutritional reserves, leading to better outcomes for subsequent children. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h6)

question: A nursing student is counseling a new mother who fears that modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility. How should the student respond?

options.A: Agree with her and advise her to avoid all modern family planning
options.B: Provide accurate, gentle education to clear up the misconception
options.C: Tell her that her fears are silly and scold her for asking
options.D: Ignore her concern and force her to accept an implant

explanation: Nurses must address common myths with patience and factual evidence to help clients make informed healthcare choices. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h6)

question: Which contraceptive method offers protection against both unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Lactational amenorrhea method
options.B: Progestin-only injectable pills
options.C: Male and female condoms
options.D: Combined oral contraceptive pills

explanation: Condoms act as physical barriers that prevent the exchange of body fluids, protecting against both pregnancy and infections. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is a key requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method to remain effective as contraception?

options.A: Taking daily iron supplements along with herbal teas
options.B: Switching to infant formula feeds after the first month
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding without supplementary feeds and no return of menses
options.D: Using male condoms during every third act of sexual intercourse

explanation: LAM relies on frequent suckling hormones to suppress ovulation, but it only works if breastfeeding is exclusive and menstruation has not resumed. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: What ethical principle ensures that a patient has the right to make their own healthcare decisions without pressure?

options.A: Paternalism
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Maleficence
options.D: Negligence

explanation: Autonomy refers to the patient's right to self-determination and independent decision-making regarding their treatment and body. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h8)

question: Why is maintaining strict confidentiality regarding family planning crucial in community nursing?

options.A: To prevent the clinic from keeping accurate statistical records
options.B: To ensure that contraceptives are sold at higher market prices
options.C: To protect clients from social stigma and domestic conflict
options.D: To hide the nurse's activities from local government leaders

explanation: Clients may face backlash or relationship issues if their contraceptive choices are shared without permission in tight-knit communities. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h8)

question: When doing home visits, what makes spotting gender-based violence different from working in a hospital?

options.A: Screening protocols are strictly enforced by hospital boards
options.B: Patients have continuous access to security personnel
options.C: Family members are legally barred from entering the room
options.D: Nurses step into private spaces where abuse can be hidden

explanation: Great job thinking about patient environments! In a home, closed doors and isolation make it much easier to hide abuse than in a busy, open hospital ward. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why do home health nurses need to watch out for non-physical abuse just as much?

options.A: Emotional abuse always leaves visible marks on medical charts
options.B: Physical abuse never occurs without emotional coercion first
options.C: Coercion, control, and isolation are core dynamics of domestic abuse
options.D: Non-physical abuse is the only type reportable by law

explanation: You've got this! Abuse isn't only physical. Emotional and psychological control can trap and break a person just as deeply as physical blows. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h1)

question: A partner stops someone from working and refuses to give them any money. What kind of abuse is this?

options.A: Psychological abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Physical abuse
options.D: Systemic abuse

explanation: Spot on! Controlling finances creates total dependence, making it very hard for a victim to walk away. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why do many victims find it so hard to leave an abusive relationship?

options.A: Physical injuries heal completely without long-term effects
options.B: Healthcare workers advise them to remain at home
options.C: Fear, financial dependence, and isolation trap them in the relationship
options.D: They genuinely enjoy the tension-building cycle

explanation: Leaving is complicated and dangerous. Fear and a lack of financial support create huge walls that keep people stuck. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which life stage is especially known for triggering or worsening domestic violence?

options.A: Adolescence
options.B: Pregnancy
options.C: Retirement
options.D: Toddlerhood

explanation: Well done! Studies show pregnancy is a high-risk period where domestic violence often starts or suddenly gets worse. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h3)

question: An older client with dementia relies totally on her son for baths and medication. Why is she at high risk for abuse?

options.A: She is exposed to many different community health workers daily
options.B: She has financial independence from her family
options.C: Her physical and cognitive dependence creates a severe power imbalance
options.D: Older adults are naturally immune to domestic coercion

explanation: Exactly. When a patient depends completely on just one person for basic daily needs, it opens the door wide to potential abuse. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which physical sign is a classic warning flag that a patient might be experiencing abuse?

options.A: A surgical scar from an appendectomy performed years ago
options.B: Unexplained bruises in various stages of healing
options.C: Age-related thinning of the skin on the forearms
options.D: Symmetrical skin rashes caused by a new soap

explanation: You got it! Bruises looking fresh, yellow, and faded all at once usually point to repeated trauma over time, not a single clumsy accident. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why might a patient give a vague, unbelievable story about a bad injury during a home visit?

options.A: Hospital guidelines discourage patients from discussing injuries
options.B: Fear of retaliation or shame often prevents them from telling the truth
options.C: Patients with chronic illness rarely remember how they get hurt
options.D: They want to test the clinical diagnostic skills of the nurse

explanation: Spot on. Fear of making things worse at home or feeling embarrassed makes many victims hide what really happened. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the absolute first safety step a nurse must take before asking a patient about abuse?

options.A: Have another nurse witness the conversation
options.B: Administer a full neurological examination
options.C: Ensure the alleged abuser is out of the room
options.D: Notify local law enforcement immediately

explanation: Safety first! Never ask screening questions in front of the suspected abuser, or you could put the patient in immediate physical danger. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h5)

question: How should a nurse document what a patient says about experiencing abuse?

options.A: Write a generalized summary to protect family privacy
options.B: Use direct quotes from the patient and record objective physical findings
options.C: Leave the information out of the chart to prevent legal complications
options.D: Record only the nursing diagnosis without patient comments

explanation: Clear and factual is best! Using direct quotes and objective notes protects the patient and builds a reliable record for future care or legal needs. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention when it comes to gender-based violence?

options.A: To treat physical injuries sustained during an attack
options.B: To prosecute offenders in a court of law
options.C: To provide emergency shelter after an assault
options.D: To stop violence before it ever occurs through education and awareness

explanation: You're doing great! Primary prevention is all about stopping violence before it even starts by teaching equality and healthy relationships. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h6)

question: How can a home health nurse practice primary prevention during routine visits?

options.A: By diagnosing psychiatric disorders in every household member
options.B: By refusing to care for households with a history of conflict
options.C: By arresting family members who display aggressive language
options.D: By modeling respectful interactions and challenging harmful stereotypes

explanation: Simple acts matter! By showing respect and speaking up against harmful views during visits, nurses help change community attitudes. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which period is known as the most dangerous time for a victim of domestic violence?

options.A: During the initial honeymoon phase of the relationship
options.B: When the victim attempts to leave or is actively leaving
options.C: Immediately after attending a routine medical checkup
options.D: When the family is sleeping through the night

explanation: Be very alert to this! The danger of severe violence or homicide spikes when an abuser feels they are losing control because the victim is leaving. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h7)

question: A patient decides to stay in an abusive home for a little longer while sorting out resources. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Collaborate with the patient to create a practical safety plan for the home
options.B: Call the police immediately to force the patient out of the house
options.C: Cancel all future home visits to avoid getting involved
options.D: Tell the patient that continuing to stay is illegal

explanation: Respect the patient's pace! Help them stay as safe as possible right where they are until they feel ready to make their move. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h7)

question: Which group is most likely covered by strict mandatory reporting laws that require action even without adult consent?

options.A: Adults with minor self-limiting acute illnesses
options.B: Older adults and individuals with severe disabilities
options.C: College students living in campus housing
options.D: Financially independent working adults

explanation: Spot on! Vulnerable groups like seniors and disabled individuals have special legal protections that mean nurses must report suspected abuse. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why is teamwork with other professionals so important in gender-based violence cases?

options.A: Nurses lack the medical training to diagnose bruises
options.B: Legal authorities handle all counseling and housing needs directly
options.C: Hospital policies prohibit nurses from talking to victims alone
options.D: Complex social, legal, and safety needs require specialized community support

explanation: You've nailed it! No single nurse can do it all. Working with social workers, legal aid, and shelters is key to helping a survivor heal. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h8)

question: What is the main focus of gerontological nursing?

options.A: Managing acute surgical emergencies in adults
options.B: Researching infectious disease outbreaks globally
options.C: Treating chronic diseases unique to childhood
options.D: Providing care specifically for older adults

explanation: You got this! Gerontological nursing is all about promoting health and providing holistic care to our older population. It's a rewarding field where you make a real difference in elderly patients' lives. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just brush off sudden confusion in an older patient as 'normal aging'?

options.A: It violates hospital discharge policies for elderly patients
options.B: It can cause the nurse to miss a treatable underlying medical problem
options.C: It always leads to immediate legal action from family members
options.D: It speeds up the natural physical decline of the brain

explanation: Never assume confusion is just old age! Sudden changes in mental status can be signs of something serious and treatable, like an infection, stroke, or delirium. Always investigate further. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h1)

question: What naturally happens to the outer layer of the skin as a person ages?

options.A: It becomes thinner and loses its elasticity
options.B: It produces significantly more sweat and oil
options.C: It permanently changes its original pigmentation
options.D: It grows thicker and develops more fat layers

explanation: As we age, our skin loses collagen and the epidermis gets thinner. This makes older adults' skin much more fragile and prone to tears or bruises. Good to keep in mind during daily care! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h2)

question: Older adults often experience stiffer chest walls and weaker breathing muscles. What is the direct result of this?

options.A: Rapid expansion of lung capacity during exercise
options.B: Total elimination of carbon dioxide from the blood
options.C: Higher residual volume and reduced vital capacity
options.D: An immediate increase in total lung surface area

explanation: Think of it like an old rubber band—stiffer chest walls and weaker muscles mean older adults can't take as deep a breath, and they trap more air in their lungs (residual volume). [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which type of mental ability actually tends to stay stable or even improve as people grow older?

options.A: Physical reaction speed during sudden emergency events
options.B: Crystallized intelligence based on accumulated life experience
options.C: Short-term working memory for complex math equations
options.D: Immediate recall of random, unrelated lists of numbers

explanation: Wisdom comes with age! Crystallized intelligence relies on stored knowledge and life experience, which stays strong or even grows as people get older. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is depression in older adults so often missed by healthcare providers?

options.A: Its symptoms are often incorrectly blamed on normal aging
options.B: Standard screening tools do not work on people over sixty
options.C: Older adults naturally have higher immunity to sadness
options.D: Depression only affects teenagers and young adults

explanation: It's easy to miss! Signs like fatigue, tiredness, and pulling away from social activities are frequently mistaken for just 'growing old,' leaving depression untreated. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a major home hazard that can cause older adults to fall?

options.A: Having too many windows in the bedroom
options.B: Loose carpets and inadequate lighting
options.C: Using electric fans during warm weather
options.D: Brightly painted walls in the hallway

explanation: Simple things like dim hallways or loose rugs are major tripping hazards. Home safety assessments are a key part of community nursing care for the elderly! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h4)

question: How can long-term social isolation negatively affect an older adult?

options.A: It stops them from developing age-related illnesses
options.B: It permanently improves their ability to stay calm
options.C: It weakens immune function and worsens mental health
options.D: It increases their daily physical endurance levels

explanation: Humans are social creatures! Lack of connection causes chronic stress, which hurts both mental well-being and the immune system. Checking in on elderly patients matters. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h4)

question: What does the clinical term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: The delivery of drugs through an intravenous line
options.B: The concurrent use of multiple medications by a patient
options.C: The process of mixing liquid medicines with food
options.D: The manufacturing of generic drugs by large pharmacies

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking several medications at once. It's very common in older adults and increases the risk of side effects and dangerous drug interactions. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are older adults especially vulnerable to bad reactions from medications?

options.A: Their liver and kidneys clear medications much more slowly
options.B: They always take their medicines at the wrong time of day
options.C: Their stomachs absorb all drugs faster than younger adults
options.D: They refuse to drink water when swallowing pills

explanation: As we age, our liver and kidneys slow down. Because they clear drugs more slowly, the medication stays in the older person's body longer and can build up to toxic levels. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of regular physical activity for older adults?

options.A: Elimination of the need for daily sleep
options.B: Complete reversal of all age-related wrinkles
options.C: Immediate restoration of lost hearing ability
options.D: Improved balance, muscle strength, and mood

explanation: Movement is medicine! Even light, tailored exercise helps seniors stay strong, lowers their risk of falls, and keeps their spirits high. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h6)

question: An older patient struggles to button their shirts because of stiff fingers from arthritis. What is the best nursing action to help them stay independent?

options.A: Insist that a family member dress the patient daily
options.B: Recommend adaptive clothing fasteners like Velcro
options.C: Tell the patient to stop wearing shirts altogether
options.D: Transfer the patient to a long-term care facility

explanation: Fantastic nursing thinking! Adaptive tools like Velcro help patients do things for themselves, boosting their confidence and maintaining their dignity. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of geriatric home healthcare?

options.A: Eliminating the need for family involvement in care
options.B: Curing all chronic illnesses through daily injections
options.C: Maintaining patient independence and safety at home
options.D: Transitioning every elderly person to a nursing facility

explanation: Geriatric home care is designed to support older adults in living safely and comfortably in their familiar home environments rather than institutional settings. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to look at the whole picture—not just a single medical diagnosis—when caring for older adults?

options.A: Because doctors usually make mistakes when diagnosing elderly patients
options.B: Because patients only care about their emotional health
options.C: Because aging affects physical, mental, and social well-being simultaneously
options.D: Because chronic diseases disappear once the home environment is changed

explanation: You've got this! Older adults often face physical, emotional, and environmental challenges all at once. Looking at the big picture helps us give the best care possible. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h1)

question: How do illnesses often show up in older adults compared to younger people?

options.A: By producing no physical changes whatsoever
options.B: With much higher fevers and severe localized pain
options.C: As subtle changes like sudden confusion or mild fatigue
options.D: Through rapid weight gain in a single day

explanation: Spot on! Older adults often show 'atypical' symptoms. Instead of a classic high fever, a simple infection might first make them unusually sleepy or confused. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main reason kidney (renal) clearance slows down as people get older?

options.A: An increase in overall heart muscle strength
options.B: Decreased physiological reserve and nephron function over time
options.C: Drinking too much clean water every day
options.D: Eating too much protein late at night

explanation: As the body ages, kidney function and blood flow naturally decrease. This is completely normal, but it means drugs and waste products take longer to leave the body. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is a very common hazard found right inside an older adult's home?

options.A: Bright overhead lighting in every room
options.B: Grab bars installed inside the shower
options.C: Low kitchen counters with wide open space
options.D: Loose scatter rugs and cluttered walkways

explanation: Simple things like loose rugs or blocked pathways are major tripping hazards that frequently lead to dangerous falls at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h3)

question: A student nurse visiting an elderly client notices a slippery bathtub with no support rails. What is the best immediate safety action?

options.A: Recommend installing grab bars and using a non-slip bath mat
options.B: Advise the client to stop bathing completely during the week
options.C: Tell the family to remodel the entire house immediately
options.D: Suggest moving the client to a hospital right away

explanation: Great choice! Adding simple items like grab bars and non-slip mats fixes the danger right away without needing drastic changes like moving out. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why are older adults at such a high risk for becoming dehydrated?

options.A: They are physically unable to swallow any liquids
options.B: Doctors usually restrict them from drinking fluids
options.C: They have a diminished sense of thirst as they age
options.D: Their bodies require less water than children do

explanation: The natural aging process can dull the body's thirst trigger, meaning seniors often just don't feel thirsty even when their bodies desperately need water. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is an effective strategy to improve nutritional intake in an older adult with poor appetite?

options.A: Waiting until the patient asks for food once a day
options.B: Serving small, nutrient-dense meals more frequently
options.C: Removing all favorite cultural foods from the diet
options.D: Forcing the patient to finish three large meals daily

explanation: Smaller meals are less overwhelming for seniors with low appetite, and making them nutrient-dense ensures they still get enough calories and vitamins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is one of the most serious risks when an older adult suffers a fall?

options.A: Severe injury and potential loss of independence
options.B: Permanent immunity from future joint pain
options.C: Immediate improvement in their overall balance
options.D: An automatic increase in their muscle strength

explanation: Falls can lead to broken bones and a lasting fear of falling again, which often strips away an older adult's ability to care for themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h5)

question: When checking a patient's walking stick (cane) or walker, what is the most important thing for you as a nurse to verify?

options.A: Instructing the patient to use it only during nighttime hours
options.B: Ensuring the device is the correct height and in good repair
options.C: Painting the frame a bright color so it looks modern
options.D: Replacing the assistive device with a wheelchair immediately

explanation: A worn-out or poorly adjusted walking aid can actually cause unsteadiness and lead to another fall. Always check the height and rubber tips! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h5)

question: In nursing, what does the term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: Storing prescription pills in a secure kitchen cabinet
options.B: The use of multiple medications by a single patient
options.C: Taking only one tablet per day for high blood pressure
options.D: Buying drugs exclusively from a wholesale pharmacy

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking many drugs at once. It's super common in older adults, but it raises the risk of side effects and drug clashes. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why are older adults much more likely to experience bad side effects from medications?

options.A: They always forget to swallow their pills with water
options.B: Their stomach acid completely destroys all medications
options.C: Their bodies metabolize and excrete medications much slower
options.D: They prefer taking herbal remedies instead of real drugs

explanation: Because liver and kidney functions slow down with age, drugs hang around in the body much longer. If doses aren't adjusted, they can easily build up to toxic levels. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which mental health condition is frequently missed in older adults because it often hides behind physical complaints like body aches?

options.A: Acute delirium
options.B: Bipolar mania
options.C: Depression
options.D: Schizophrenia

explanation: Good to know! Depression in seniors is easy to miss because they might talk about constant tiredness or aches instead of feeling sad. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the main advantage of using validation therapy with a patient who has dementia?

options.A: It forces the patient to remember exact dates and times
options.B: It proves to the patient that their memories are false
options.C: It cures the underlying brain disease within a few weeks
options.D: It acknowledges their feelings and helps reduce agitation

explanation: Instead of arguing with a confused patient, validation therapy respects their feelings. This keeps them calm, safe, and feeling understood. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for older adults with advanced illnesses?

options.A: Quickly discharging the patient from home care
options.B: Maximizing comfort and quality of life
options.C: Stopping all forms of nursing communication
options.D: Finding a complete cure for every diagnosis

explanation: Palliative care isn't about curing; it's all about easing pain and distressing symptoms so the patient can live their remaining days with dignity and comfort. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why is supporting family caregivers considered such a vital part of home healthcare?

options.A: To prevent caregiver burnout and maintain safe care at home
options.B: Because family members replace the doctor in writing prescriptions
options.C: To ensure the family pays for all medical supplies out of pocket
options.D: Because nurses are not allowed to visit patients alone

explanation: Caring for a sick relative is exhausting. By supporting family caregivers, we protect their health and ensure they can keep providing safe care at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h8)

question: What does a healthy healing wound bed look like when it's doing well?

options.A: Black and hard
options.B: Yellow and stringy
options.C: Bright red and moist
options.D: Pale white and dry

explanation: You're doing great! Healthy healing tissue (granulation tissue) is packed with fresh blood vessels, giving it a bright red, shiny, and moist look that shows healing is well underway. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why do nurses check the skin right around a wound (the periwound area), not just the wound itself?

options.A: It determines how much protein the patient needs in their diet.
options.B: It dictates the exact brand of dressing the doctor must prescribe.
options.C: It shows if drainage or moisture is damaging the healthy skin around the wound.
options.D: It helps calculate the exact surface area in square centimeters.

explanation: Spotting issues early around the wound helps you catch irritation or moisture damage before the wound starts getting bigger. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h1)

question: What level of technique is normally used when changing chronic wound dressings at home?

options.A: Clean technique
options.B: Surgical sterility
options.C: Chemical disinfection only
options.D: Complete germ-free isolation

explanation: For routine home care, clean technique is the standard! It relies on solid hand hygiene and clean tools rather than trying to keep things operating-room sterile. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good step when setting up a clean workspace on a household table?

options.A: Washing your hands thoroughly before touching any supplies
options.B: Using a clean disposable barrier like a paper towel as your work surface
options.C: Keeping clean supplies separate from used or dirty items
options.D: Spraying the table with a standard household bleach solution right before laying down sterile instruments

explanation: Spray bottles and wet chemicals right next to open supplies can easily contaminate your clean field. Using a dry paper towel barrier is much safer! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which dressing works best for a wound that has heavy bleeding or fluid drainage?

options.A: Dry gauze pad
options.B: Transparent film
options.C: Hydrocolloid wafer
options.D: Alginate dressing

explanation: Alginates come from seaweed and are superstars at soaking up lots of fluid while turning into a soft gel that keeps the wound bed happy. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h3)

question: When packing a deep wound in a patient's home, what is the golden rule for placing the gauze inside?

options.A: Pack the wound tightly until it is completely firm to stop all bleeding.
options.B: Pack the wound loosely so it fills the space without putting pressure on the tissue.
options.C: Pack the wound using dry cotton balls for maximum absorption.
options.D: Pack only the top layer of skin and leave the deeper cavity empty.

explanation: Remember: never pack too tightly! Packing a wound too firmly cuts off the blood supply those new cells need to heal. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h3)

question: What should you do first if an old sticky dressing won't budge from a wound bed?

options.A: Moisten it slightly with sterile saline to loosen it gently
options.B: Soak the entire limb in a bucket of tap water
options.C: Cut the skin around the tape to remove it
options.D: Pull it off quickly in one sharp motion to save time

explanation: A little saline goes a long way. Moistening a stuck dressing protects delicate new tissue and keeps your patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do nurses clean a wound starting from the center and wiping outward?

options.A: It makes the cleaning solution spread evenly across the room.
options.B: It stops the patient from feeling ticklish during the procedure.
options.C: It speeds up how fast the skin cells can multiply.
options.D: It prevents pushing bacteria from the surrounding skin back into the wound bed.

explanation: Think of the center as the cleanest zone. Wiping outward ensures you don't drag outside germs back into the healing tissue! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which sign clearly points to a worsening wound infection?

options.A: Mild itching around the edge of the tape
options.B: Firm, pink tissue filling the wound base
options.C: Foul-smelling, purulent drainage and spreading redness
options.D: A thin layer of clear, watery fluid on the surface

explanation: Pus, a bad smell, and redness that creeps outward are classic red flags that bacteria are taking over and causing an active infection. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h5)

question: A patient's abdominal surgical wound suddenly pops open and loop of bowel peeks out. What is your immediate action?

options.A: Apply an ice pack to the exposed tissue to reduce swelling
options.B: Wait until the scheduled doctor appointment next week to report it
options.C: Cover the area with sterile saline-moistened dressings and call for emergency help
options.D: Gently push the bowel back inside the abdomen and tape it shut

explanation: This is an emergency called evisceration! Keep the organs moist with sterile saline dressings and call for emergency help right away—never push them back in. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is a 'return demonstration' the best way to see if a family caregiver knows how to do a dressing change?

options.A: It replaces the need to document anything in the patient chart.
options.B: It allows the nurse to leave the home early while the family works.
options.C: It ensures the family buys the most expensive medical supplies.
options.D: It proves they can physically perform the steps correctly rather than just nodding yes.

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them do it in front of you ensures they really understand the steps, way better than just taking their word for it. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the main role of a home care nurse when working with the healthcare team on a slow-healing wound?

options.A: Acting as the eyes and ears to report accurate, up-to-date wound changes to providers
options.B: Ordering all prescription medications without physician approval
options.C: Performing surgical debridement during every home visit
options.D: Diagnosing the underlying systemic disease independently

explanation: You are the vital link! Your accurate updates from the home help doctors, dietitians, and specialists adjust the care plan so the patient heals faster. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)

question: What are Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) mostly about?

options.A: Community mobility and grocery shopping
options.B: Basic self-care tasks needed for daily survival
options.C: Complex household chores and managing money
options.D: Advanced professional skills and hobbies

explanation: You've got this! ADLs are simply the fundamental things we do every day to care for ourselves, like bathing, dressing, and eating. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of these shows a patient is having trouble with the ADL of 'transferring'?

options.A: The patient forgets to add sugar to their tea.
options.B: The patient cannot balance their monthly bills.
options.C: The patient wears mismatched socks and unbuttoned shirts.
options.D: The patient needs help moving from the bed to a chair.

explanation: Spot on! In nursing, 'transferring' is all about safely moving a patient from one surface to another, like from a bed to a wheelchair. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h1)

question: How do Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs) differ from basic ADLs?

options.A: IADLs involve more complex tasks needed to live independently in the community.
options.B: IADLs require no thinking, just muscle strength.
options.C: IADLs are learned before basic self-care.
options.D: IADLs only focus on physical hygiene.

explanation: Think of basic ADLs as surviving day-to-day, while IADLs are the next level up—like cooking, shopping, and handling money—that help someone live on their own. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h2)

question: A patient forgets to take their blood pressure meds and misses paying their utility bills. Which daily skill area is struggling?

options.A: Involuntary body reflexes
options.B: Gross motor developmental milestones
options.C: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs)
options.D: Basic self-care ADLs

explanation: Well done! Managing medications and paying bills require a bit more brainpower and planning, which puts them right into the IADL category. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main reason nurses use tools like the Katz Index and Lawton Scale?

options.A: To calculate how many calories an older adult needs
options.B: To diagnose specific brain diseases like Alzheimer's
options.C: To test the physical strength of a patient's arms
options.D: To measure a patient's independence and what care they need

explanation: Exactly! These scoring tools give us a clear, objective picture of what a patient can do on their own and where they might need a helping hand. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h3)

question: A nurse wants to check if an elderly patient can safely cook and manage money at home. Which tool should she use?

options.A: Katz ADL Index
options.B: Braden Scale for Pressure Ulcers
options.C: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.D: Lawton IADL Scale

explanation: Spot on! The Lawton scale is specifically built to assess those higher-level, independent living skills like cooking and managing finances. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do memory or brain issues usually affect IADLs before basic ADLs?

options.A: Patients always get more help with cooking than bathing.
options.B: IADLs require higher-level thinking and complex planning.
options.C: Basic ADLs depend entirely on memory, not muscles.
options.D: Brain changes never affect physical self-care.

explanation: You got it! Tasks like budgeting or sorting meds need sharp executive brain function, which is often the first thing to be affected when memory starts to slip. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical chronic condition that threatens an older adult's independence?

options.A: Mild seasonal allergies
options.B: Diabetic nerve damage
options.C: Heart failure
options.D: Stroke

explanation: That's right! While allergies can be annoying, they don't cause long-term disability like major strokes, heart issues, or nerve damage do. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h4)

question: How do assistive devices and home changes mainly help a patient whose health is declining?

options.A: By completely removing the need for a nurse
options.B: By bridging the gap between needing help and safe independence
options.C: By replacing lost brain function from dementia
options.D: By curing underlying chronic illnesses

explanation: Brilliant! Tools and modifications are all about helping patients squeeze out every bit of independence they safely can. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h5)

question: An older patient keeps losing their balance when standing up from the toilet. What should the nurse suggest first?

options.A: Buying a complex electronic pill dispenser
options.B: Giving them a high-dose stimulant
options.C: Moving their bedroom upstairs
options.D: Installing secure grab bars near the toilet

explanation: Safety first! Grab bars provide immediate, physical support right where they need it during risky moves like standing up. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is a major sign that a family caregiver is experiencing burnout?

options.A: Going out more often to social clubs
options.B: Complete indifference to the patient's schedule
options.C: Sudden muscle gains and athletic strength
options.D: Chronic tiredness, emotional exhaustion, and poor sleep

explanation: Spot on. Caregiving is tough work, and without breaks, it can easily lead to deep physical and mental exhaustion. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is teaching safe body mechanics to family caregivers such an important nursing duty?

options.A: It cures chronic illnesses in the patient.
options.B: It protects the patient from falls and the caregiver from back injuries.
options.C: It cuts down the monthly grocery bill.
options.D: It gets rid of the need for grab bars.

explanation: You nailed it! Good lifting habits keep both the helper's back safe and the patient secure during transfers. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of doing a health assessment right inside a patient's home?

options.A: To enforce strict hospital rules in a private residential property
options.B: To evaluate how well a person manages their health in their daily living space
options.C: To replace the need for routine visits to the primary doctor
options.D: To test family members on basic nursing and medical procedures

explanation: Spot on! Home assessments help us see how patients truly cope with their health right where they live every day. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why does visiting a patient's home often reveal health details that a clinic visit misses?

options.A: Clinic doctors lack the training to ask patients about their daily habits.
options.B: Hospital staff deliberately hide dietary information from visiting relatives.
options.C: Patients cannot remember their medical history when they leave their house.
options.D: Seeing the home environment uncovers hidden barriers to proper self-care.

explanation: You got it! Walking into their space lets you spot real-life challenges—like a lack of food or unsafe furniture—that they might forget to mention at the clinic. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common fall hazard found in many homes?

options.A: Loose scatter rugs on polished floors
options.B: Low furniture located near the walls
options.C: Hardwood floors without any coverings
options.D: Bright lighting in the hallway stairs

explanation: Exactly! Unsecured rugs easily slip underfoot, making them a leading cause of accidental falls at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h2)

question: You walk into an older patient's living room and see an extension cord stretched tightly across the main pathway. What should you do?

options.A: Instruct the patient to tape the cord down with masking tape.
options.B: Recommend moving the cord out of the pathway to prevent a fall.
options.C: Report the patient to local housing authorities for a safety violation.
options.D: Ignore the cord since it supplies power to a necessary lamp.

explanation: Spot on! Clearing tripping hazards from walkways keeps your patient safe from preventable injuries. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why is it tricky to use a stethoscope when a patient is lying on a very soft home bed?

options.A: Patients usually fall asleep immediately upon lying down on them.
options.B: Soft mattresses absorb all the sound waves from the stethoscope.
options.C: It makes proper patient positioning and organ assessment difficult.
options.D: Soft beds prevent the nurse from checking the patient's radial pulse.

explanation: Well done! A soft, unsupportive bed makes it hard to keep the correct posture needed to properly listen to the chest and tummy. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h3)

question: What should you do if a patient's room is too dark when you are trying to check their skin?

options.A: Ask the patient to turn on all the household television sets.
options.B: Use a portable examination light to properly view the skin.
options.C: Skip the skin inspection until the patient visits the clinic.
options.D: Rely entirely on touch and palpation to detect any skin rashes.

explanation: Correct! Good lighting is a must for spotting subtle rashes, bruises, or color changes that you'd miss in a dark room. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following tasks is classified as an Activity of Daily Living?

options.A: Banking
options.B: Bathing
options.C: Cooking
options.D: Shopping

explanation: Activities of Daily Living are basic self-care tasks required for personal independence, which include bathing, dressing, eating, and toileting. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is watching a patient actually do a household task better than just asking if they can do it?

options.A: Patients often lie to nurses to avoid being sent away to a hospital.
options.B: Verbal reports may not match the patient's actual physical capability.
options.C: Patients forget the names of the tools they use for cooking and cleaning.
options.D: Direct observation is a mandatory legal requirement in all provinces.

explanation: Spot on! People often overestimate what they can do or try to hide their struggles, so watching them yourself gives you the true picture. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the very first practical step when doing medication reconciliation during a home visit?

options.A: Calling the local pharmacy to order a fresh supply of all tablets
options.B: Gathering all current medication bottles and packages into one place
options.C: Asking the doctor to rewrite every prescription from the beginning
options.D: Throwing away any medicine that does not have a readable label

explanation: You got it! You have to round up all the medications first so you can actually see what the patient has and is taking. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h5)

question: A patient with mild arthritis struggles to open childproof medicine caps, so they leave bottles wide open on the table. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Advise the patient to use a hammer to break the stubborn plastic caps.
options.B: Take all the medication away and manage it from the nursing office.
options.C: Recommend easy-open non-childproof caps if no young children visit.
options.D: Scold the patient for leaving dangerous chemicals out in the open.

explanation: Brilliant! Making medicine packaging accessible helps them stay compliant with their treatment without risking injury from stubborn caps. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is checking skin elasticity (turgor) alone not a reliable way to check for dehydration in an older adult?

options.A: Older adults always refuse to let nurses pinch their hands or arms.
options.B: Aging skin naturally loses elasticity, making it look dehydrated even when it is normal.
options.C: Skin turgor only measures protein levels, not the body's water content.
options.D: Older adults produce too much natural sweat to measure skin fluid accurately.

explanation: Spot on! Older skin naturally loses its bounce, so it can look 'tented' even when the person is well-hydrated. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a classic physical sign that a patient is mildly dehydrated?

options.A: Clear and copious urine output
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and dark urine
options.C: Excessive saliva production in the mouth
options.D: Swollen ankles and high blood pressure

explanation: Correct! When fluid is low, the mouth gets dry and the kidneys concentrate urine, turning it dark. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h6)

question: What type of language should a nurse use when writing home care notes?

options.A: Brief and casual phrases to save time
options.B: Objective, specific, and measurable details
options.C: General summaries and personal opinions
options.D: Emotional descriptions of the family dynamic

explanation: You got it! Stick to clear, factual observations so any other nurse reading your notes knows the exact status of the patient. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why is accurate home care documentation especially critical compared to hospital notes?

options.A: Hospital records are destroyed as soon as the patient is discharged.
options.B: Insurance companies never read hospital charts, only home visit notes.
options.C: Home patients are legally required to keep a copy of every nurse's note.
options.D: Home nurses work independently and their notes are the main record of care.

explanation: Spot on! Since home nurses work on their own without a team standing right beside them, detailed notes are vital for tracking progress safely. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h7)

question: When doing a home nutrition check, besides looking at physical health, what is a key thing to inspect?

options.A: Prescribing vitamin supplements to the family
options.B: Inspecting available food in the pantry
options.C: Weighing the patient once every month
options.D: Ordering laboratory blood tests immediately

explanation: Spot on! Checking the pantry and fridge helps you see the actual food the patient can reach and eat at home. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is checking out the home environment so important for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will eat all prescribed meals
options.B: It reveals practical barriers like trouble with grocery shopping
options.C: It proves whether the family is hiding food from the patient
options.D: It replaces the need to check the patient's weight

explanation: Exactly! Home visits show you real-life challenges, like physical issues that make buying or cooking food hard. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h1)

question: Losing how much weight unintentionally in a single month is a major red flag for malnutrition?

options.A: Any weight loss at all
options.B: More than five percent
options.C: Ten pounds regardless of body size
options.D: Exactly one percent

explanation: Great job! Dropping over 5% of your body weight in a month is a serious warning sign that needs quick attention. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h2)

question: How does bad dental health often lead to poor nutrition in elderly home care patients?

options.A: It makes chewing painful, causing them to avoid tough, nutritious foods
options.B: It causes immediate weight gain due to poor digestion
options.C: It destroys the taste buds permanently
options.D: It blocks the absorption of vitamins in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! When teeth or dentures hurt, patients naturally switch to soft foods, which can sometimes miss out on key nutrients. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main reason special diets must respect a patient's culture?

options.A: To speed up the healing of surgical wounds
options.B: To ensure the patient actually eats the food provided
options.C: To reduce the cost of buying groceries
options.D: To prevent allergic reactions in the home

explanation: You got it! If a meal plan ignores a patient's cultural tastes, they simply won't eat it, leading to poor nutrition. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h3)
