question: What is a major goal of skilled care when looking after someone with a long-term, chronic illness?

options.A: Elimination of all daily living assistance needs.
options.B: Complete permanent cure of the underlying disease.
options.C: Immediate discharge back to independent living.
options.D: Stabilization, symptom relief, and functional preservation.

explanation: When a chronic condition can't be cured, our goal shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, managing symptoms, and helping them stay as active as possible. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why must nurses balance medical treatments with a resident's personal wishes?

options.A: To avoid documenting any clinical changes in the chart.
options.B: To ensure the patient performs all physical therapy alone.
options.C: To respect resident dignity while still achieving safe, effective outcomes.
options.D: To completely bypass hospital discharge regulations.

explanation: Person-centered care means we team up with our patients, respecting what they value while keeping them safe and healthy. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which of these nursing duties counts as a skilled nursing intervention?

options.A: Managing complex wound care and dressing changes.
options.B: Assisting a resident with walking down the hallway.
options.C: Handing out meal trays to all residents at lunchtime.
options.D: Helping a resident put on their casual daytime clothes.

explanation: Wound care needs professional clinical technique and assessment, making it a true skilled nursing task! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h3)

question: A patient with a new tracheostomy needs airway suctioning. Why is this considered skilled care?

options.A: It is a basic personal hygiene task that any family member can perform.
options.B: It replaces the need for daily medication administration.
options.C: It is only performed once a year during an annual physical exam.
options.D: It requires specialized clinical knowledge to prevent airway occlusion and infection.

explanation: Keeping an airway clear takes specialized training and sharp monitoring to stop dangerous complications like breathing trouble. Excellent work! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of the registered nurse inside a healthcare team?

options.A: Replacing the dietician for meal planning and kitchen duties.
options.B: Providing all physical therapy exercises without therapist assistance.
options.C: Prescribing new medications when the doctor is off duty.
options.D: Acting as the clinical hub to coordinate care among all disciplines.

explanation: As nurses, we bring the whole healthcare team together so everyone is on the same page for the patient's care. You're mastering teamwork! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why is teamwork among different health professionals so vital in a nursing facility?

options.A: It prevents fragmented care and addresses the resident's total health needs.
options.B: It reduces the total number of staff required on every shift.
options.C: It allows nurses to avoid communicating directly with resident families.
options.D: It eliminates the need for any written nursing documentation.

explanation: When doctors, nurses, therapists, and dieticians work hand in hand, nothing falls through the cracks for the resident. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h4)

question: What tool is commonly used in skilled care settings to assess and track resident health status?

options.A: Minimum Data Set (MDS)
options.B: Pediatric growth chart
options.C: Surgical safety checklist
options.D: Emergency room triage scale

explanation: The Minimum Data Set (MDS) is a standard assessment tool used in long-term care facilities to evaluate how a resident is doing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why do we say a resident's care plan must be treated as a living document?

options.A: It is legally required to be rewritten word-for-word every single morning.
options.B: It is only used during the initial admission interview and never again.
options.C: It must be adjusted whenever the resident's clinical condition changes.
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to document daily shift assessments.

explanation: A resident's health changes day by day, so their care plan needs to grow and update right along with them. Spot on! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why must nurses watch out for medication build-up in older adults receiving skilled care?

options.A: Renal and hepatic function always improve with advanced age.
options.B: Decreased kidney and liver function can lead to drug accumulation and toxicity.
options.C: Older adults process all drugs much faster than younger adults do.
options.D: Medications have no side effects once a patient enters a nursing home.

explanation: As the body ages, the kidneys and liver naturally slow down a bit. This means drugs stay in the system longer, so we have to watch for toxic build-up. Brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h6)

question: An older resident taking blood pressure pills suddenly feels dizzy and takes a fall. What should the nurse think of first?

options.A: An immediate need to discharge the resident home.
options.B: The complete absence of any pharmacological influence.
options.C: A normal reaction that requires no clinical follow-up.
options.D: A potential adverse drug reaction or cumulative medication effect.

explanation: Dizziness and sudden falls in older adults are classic clues that a medication might be lowering their blood pressure too much or making them drowsy. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of restorative nursing programs in skilled facilities?

options.A: To maintain functional gains achieved during formal therapy sessions.
options.B: To provide custodial care without any medical oversight.
options.C: To replace physical therapists entirely for every resident.
options.D: To eliminate all physical activity for frail residents.

explanation: Restorative care helps residents practice what they learned in therapy so they don't lose their hard-earned progress! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why should nurses encourage residents to do tasks for themselves whenever they can?

options.A: To punish residents who refuse to participate in group activities.
options.B: To allow nursing staff to take longer breaks during the day.
options.C: To prevent rapid physical deconditioning and preserve independence.
options.D: To reduce the total amount of paperwork required for the shift.

explanation: Encouraging self-care keeps muscles strong and helps residents hold onto their independence and confidence. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why is clear, objective nursing documentation so crucial in skilled care facilities?

options.A: It is only used by insurance companies to deny resident coverage.
options.B: It guarantees that no resident will ever experience a fall.
options.C: It serves as a legal safeguard and proves that skilled criteria were met.
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers between nurses.

explanation: Good charting is your best friend! It acts as a legal proof that the resident truly needed and received expert nursing care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h8)

question: How do quality improvement teams use data like fall rates and skin injury reports?

options.A: To hide negative clinical outcomes from state regulatory agencies.
options.B: To track performance trends and guide system-wide safety improvements.
options.C: To find individual nurses to blame whenever an accident happens.
options.D: To determine which residents should be discharged immediately.

explanation: Quality improvement isn't about blaming people—it's about spotting trends so we can make our hospital or facility safer for everyone! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h8)

question: What is the primary focus of custodial care?

options.A: Acute stabilization of sudden emergency conditions
options.B: Administering intravenous medications and complex therapies
options.C: Providing non-medical support for daily living needs
options.D: Surgical interventions for chronic disease management

explanation: Custodial care is specifically structured around non-medical assistance rather than clinical or curative procedures. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: A stable elderly patient needs help with eating and bathing at home. Which care type is most appropriate?

options.A: Intensive care
options.B: Custodial care
options.C: Surgical nursing
options.D: Emergency triage

explanation: Assistance with basic daily routines for a stable individual falls squarely under the umbrella of custodial care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: Moving a client safely from a hospital bed to a wheelchair is classified as which activity?

options.A: Dressing
options.B: Transferring
options.C: Toileting
options.D: Feeding

explanation: Transferring refers to the physical movement of a patient from one surface or posture to another. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h2)

question: A patient struggles to button shirts and tie shoes due to severe hand arthritis. This represents a deficit in which area?

options.A: Bathing
options.B: Continence
options.C: Feeding
options.D: Dressing

explanation: Clothing selection and fastening garments are core components of dressing activities. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which task requires skilled nursing rather than custodial care?

options.A: Administering intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.B: Assisting a client with eating a midday meal
options.C: Supervising a walk around the backyard
options.D: Helping an elderly person put on slippers

explanation: Intravenous medication administration is a clinical intervention that requires nursing licensing and pharmacological knowledge. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is the distinction between skilled nursing and custodial care important for healthcare planning?

options.A: It proves that family members can perform complex surgical procedures
options.B: It determines the appropriate type of personnel and resource allocation needed
options.C: It eliminates the need for any ongoing patient assessment at home
options.D: It shows that all chronic patients eventually require intensive care units

explanation: Knowing the care category ensures that patients receive the correct level of professional staffing and support. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h3)

question: The primary role of a home health aide in custodial care is to:

options.A: Assist with personal hygiene and daily routines
options.B: Perform independent medical diagnoses and treatment
options.C: Prescribe maintenance medications for chronic illnesses
options.D: Perform major surgical procedures in the home

explanation: Home health aides focus on supporting personal hygiene, mobility, and basic daily living needs. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h4)

question: A family caregiver caring for an immobile relative at home is showing signs of physical exhaustion and irritability. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assess the caregiver for burnout and discuss respite care options
options.B: Report the family member to social services for negligence immediately
options.C: Advise the client to dismiss the family caregiver from the home
options.D: Tell the family member that caring for relatives is mandatory

explanation: Recognizing caregiver fatigue requires introducing supportive measures like respite care to maintain safety for both parties. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a turning schedule for a bedridden patient?

options.A: Reducing the need for nursing documentation
options.B: Increasing the patient's daily caloric intake
options.C: Accelerating the healing of bone fractures
options.D: Preventing the development of pressure ulcers

explanation: Repositioning clients at regular intervals relieves constant pressure on bony prominences, protecting skin integrity. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h5)

question: Removing loose rugs and adding grab bars in the bathroom primarily helps to achieve what goal?

options.A: Lowering the financial cost of home healthcare
options.B: Improving the clinical accuracy of medication dosing
options.C: Reducing the risk of falls and environmental injuries
options.D: Eliminating the need for any physical assistance

explanation: Environmental modifications directly target physical safety by removing common household hazards. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h5)

question: How is long-term custodial care primarily funded for most families in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory employer-paid private disability policies
options.B: Comprehensive national health insurance schemes
options.C: Free government-provided universal home care
options.D: Out-of-pocket spending and family networks

explanation: Most long-term non-medical care relies on personal funds and support from extended family structures. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why should nurses be familiar with local NGOs and community resources when planning custodial care?

options.A: To bypass hospital physicians when prescribing controlled drugs
options.B: To secure government funding for personal nursing salaries
options.C: To delegate all nursing responsibilities to external volunteers
options.D: To help families find financial and material assistance for long-term needs

explanation: Community resources help bridge the gap created by limited insurance coverage for non-medical long-term care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: What was the main purpose of early almshouses and poorhouses?

options.A: To provide advanced surgical and medical treatments
options.B: To train the first generation of registered nurses
options.C: To serve as specialized retirement homes for the wealthy
options.D: To shelter the destitute, elderly, and chronically ill

explanation: Think of early almshouses as general community shelters. They were set up to care for people who had no one else, like the poor and frail elderly, long before modern hospitals and nursing homes existed! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why were early almshouses poorly suited for caring for the sick and elderly?

options.A: They suffered from severe overcrowding and a lack of medical staff
options.B: They charged fees that only wealthy families could afford
options.C: They focused too heavily on expensive experimental therapies
options.D: They refused to admit anyone over the age of fifty

explanation: These places were often jam-packed and lacked trained health workers. Mixing different vulnerable people together without proper medical care meant chronic illnesses weren't managed well. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which post-WWII law provided funding for hospital construction and indirectly led to the growth of nursing homes?

options.A: The Social Security Amendment
options.B: The Medicare and Medicaid Act
options.C: The Nursing Home Reform Act
options.D: The Hill-Burton Act

explanation: The Hill-Burton Act funded a massive wave of hospital building. Once those hospitals started discharging patients who still needed long-term care, the need for separate nursing homes became super obvious! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h2)

question: How did the post-WWII era change the main reason why nursing homes were opened?

options.A: Religious organizations closed all facilities to focus solely on home nursing
options.B: Communities stopped caring for older adults outside of acute hospitals
options.C: Governments took direct control of all private health institutions
options.D: Eldercare shifted from a charitable or public welfare function into a commercial business

explanation: With hospitals discharging more chronically ill older adults, private business owners saw a chance to step in and turn eldercare into a profitable commercial venture. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which government program became the main payer for long-term nursing home care after 1965?

options.A: Medicare
options.B: The Hill-Burton fund
options.C: Social Security
options.D: Medicaid

explanation: Medicaid was built to support low-income individuals, and over time it grew to become the primary financial backbone paying for long-term stays in nursing facilities. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h3)

question: A newly opened nursing home focuses entirely on packing in as many residents as possible to maximize government payouts. Based on trends from the 1960s and 70s, what is a likely result?

options.A: Excessive funding directly spent on recreational programs
options.B: Compromised quality of resident care and severe staff burnout
options.C: Immediate elimination of all chronic health conditions
options.D: Universal praise from visiting public health inspectors

explanation: When a facility chases high numbers over quality care, they usually cut corners on staffing. This leaves nurses overworked and patients getting less-than-ideal attention. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h3)

question: What major change did the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 introduce regarding resident management?

options.A: It removed all requirements for regular state health inspections
options.B: It placed severe restrictions on the use of physical and chemical restraints
options.C: It encouraged facilities to lock residents in rooms for safety
options.D: It mandated that all residents must take daily sedative medications

explanation: The 1987 law stepped in because restraints were often used just to make life easier for staff rather than keeping patients safe. The law heavily cracked down on this practice! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why was the Minimum Data Set (MDS) introduced as part of the 1987 reforms?

options.A: To determine which staff members should be terminated each quarter
options.B: To standardize comprehensive resident assessments and guide individualized care planning
options.C: To calculate the exact profit margins for private facility owners
options.D: To track how many visitors each resident received every week

explanation: The MDS is a fantastic tool for nurses! It ensures every resident gets a thorough health assessment so the team can build a care plan tailored specifically to that person's needs. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of person-centered care in modern long-term facilities?

options.A: To honor individual resident preferences, choices, and daily routines
options.B: To reduce operating costs by standardizing all resident meals
options.C: To enforce strict schedules that make facility operations more efficient
options.D: To eliminate the need for any licensed nursing staff on site

explanation: Person-centered care puts the resident first! Instead of forcing everyone onto a rigid hospital schedule, it revolves around what the individual patient actually likes and prefers. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h5)

question: How does assisted living differ fundamentally from traditional skilled nursing homes?

options.A: It provides a homelike environment that emphasizes autonomy and help with daily tasks rather than heavy medical care
options.B: It relies entirely on family members to provide all professional nursing services
options.C: It refuses admission to any older adult who has a chronic medical condition
options.D: It operates strictly as a hospital ward for patients requiring mechanical ventilation

explanation: Assisted living is meant for folks who just need a little boost with daily activities (like bathing or dressing) but don't need round-the-clock intensive medical nursing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is a major workforce challenge currently facing the long-term care industry?

options.A: An overabundance of licensed nurses competing for very few open beds
options.B: Mandatory retirement ages that force nurses to leave the field early
options.C: Severe staff shortages and high burnout rates among nurses and aides
options.D: Strict laws prohibiting nurses from working in residential settings

explanation: It's no secret that long-term care can be tough. Low pay, heavy workloads, and physical demands mean keeping and recruiting enough nurses remains a major hurdle. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of innovative 'small-house' models in modern nursing care?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any professional healthcare oversight
options.B: To lower building construction costs by using temporary tents
options.C: To break large, sterile institutions down into homelike residential units
options.D: To reduce the total number of older adults requiring assistance worldwide

explanation: Small-house models ditch the long, intimidating hospital hallways and replace them with cozy, home-style spaces where residents can build genuine community connections. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of an assisted living facility?

options.A: Serving as a permanent substitute for acute hospital stays
options.B: Housing only individuals with severe mental health disorders
options.C: Providing support for daily tasks while keeping independence
options.D: Offering around-the-clock intensive medical and surgical care

explanation: Assisted living is designed for people who need some help with daily living but do not require heavy nursing care, allowing them to remain as independent as possible. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: How do assisted living facilities differ from traditional nursing homes?

options.A: Assisted living requires continuous 24-hour physician supervision.
options.B: Nursing homes provide much less medical oversight than assisted living.
options.C: Nursing homes only admit individuals who are completely independent.
options.D: Assisted living focuses more on a home-like setting and independence.

explanation: While nursing homes offer heavy, continuous medical and nursing care, assisted living emphasizes residential comfort and autonomy with lesser medical intervention. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is evaluated during a functional assessment prior to admission?

options.A: Financial credit history
options.B: Workplace performance record
options.C: Previous travel experiences
options.D: Activities of daily living

explanation: A functional assessment looks closely at how well a potential resident can manage basic daily self-care tasks like bathing and dressing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: A client with advanced dementia who wanders at night is being checked into an assisted living facility that does not have a secure memory unit. What should the facility do?

options.A: Wait until the client's memory improves on its own
options.B: Deny admission because the facility cannot keep the client safe
options.C: Admit the client and just use door chimes for night safety
options.D: Accept the client and assign a private nurse paid by the family

explanation: You've got this! Facilities must match their care to what the client genuinely needs. Admitting a wandering client to an unsecure place creates a big safety risk. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: Which service is typically included as a core offering in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Complex intravenous chemotherapy administration
options.B: Intensive care unit mechanical ventilation
options.C: Major orthopedic surgical procedures
options.D: Assistance with daily personal hygiene and bathing

explanation: Personal care assistance with hygiene, dressing, and bathing forms the core foundation of daily services in assisted living. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why do care staff encourage residents to do parts of their morning routine all by themselves?

options.A: To reduce the total number of staff members needed on duty
options.B: To eliminate the need for any individualized service plans
options.C: To comply with federal acute care hospital regulations
options.D: To prevent physical decline caused by lack of use

explanation: Great thinking! Letting residents do what they can manage preserves their muscle strength, coordination, and sense of pride. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a nurse working in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Managing hospital emergency room admissions
options.B: Monitoring health status and coordinating care services
options.C: Running the facility financial and accounting department
options.D: Performing major surgical operations on-site

explanation: Assisted living nurses focus on health monitoring, wellness checks, and coordinating various support and medical services for the residents. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h4)

question: How is the role of a nurse in assisted living different from a nurse in a busy hospital?

options.A: Assisted living nurses focus more on wellness, supervision, and chronic care coordination.
options.B: Acute care nurses have no responsibility for monitoring patient vital signs.
options.C: Assisted living nurses provide continuous one-on-one surgical recovery care.
options.D: Acute care nurses never supervise nursing assistants.

explanation: Spot on! While hospital nurses handle unstable, emergency conditions, assisted living nurses focus on long-term wellness, chronic care, and guiding support staff. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the document used by staff to track when medications are given to residents?

options.A: Maintenance repair schedule
options.B: Medication administration record
options.C: Facility financial balance sheet
options.D: Daily dietary menu log

explanation: The medication administration record, or MAR, is the official document used to track every dose of medication given to a resident. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: A resident says they already took their morning blood pressure pill, but the medication administration record (MAR) is blank for that time. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a second dose immediately to ensure their blood pressure stays controlled
options.B: Wait until the evening shift to see if the blood pressure spikes
options.C: Assume the resident is correct and sign the record as given by the resident
options.D: Withhold the dose and consult the prescribing physician or charge nurse before acting

explanation: Brilliant! Giving a double dose can be dangerous. Always pause, check the facts, and consult your senior colleagues or doctor when something doesn't match up. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a key benefit of offering structured social activities in assisted living?

options.A: Replacing the need for family visits altogether
options.B: Reducing the cost of building maintenance
options.C: Combating feelings of loneliness and depression
options.D: Eliminating the need for any routine medical care

explanation: Group activities and social events help keep residents engaged, active, and emotionally connected, reducing isolation and depression. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why is it important for assisted living homes to balance safety rules with personal freedom?

options.A: Residents who experience freedom no longer require medical care.
options.B: Federal laws prohibit any facility from locking doors or windows.
options.C: Excessive rules can strip away a resident's dignity and sense of home.
options.D: Safety protocols have no impact on the mental health of older adults.

explanation: You've got this! Safety matters, but making a home feel like a strict prison hurts residents' happiness and takes away their independence. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which government body is mainly responsible for inspecting and licensing assisted living facilities?

options.A: State health or social services departments
options.B: Federal military defense agencies
options.C: International travel and tourism boards
options.D: National automotive safety councils

explanation: State health departments set the rules, run routine checks, and make sure assisted living homes follow health and safety laws. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h7)

question: What must an assisted living facility do after inspectors find a safety or rule violation during a visit?

options.A: Submit and implement a formal plan of correction
options.B: Immediately close the building and relocate all residents
options.C: Change the state laws to match current facility practices
options.D: Ignore the finding if staff members disagree with it

explanation: Spot on! When inspectors find a problem, the facility has to write down a clear plan showing how they will fix it and make sure it never happens again. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of an adult day care home?

options.A: To offer permanent residential housing for older adults
options.B: To serve as a 24-hour acute care hospital ward
options.C: To provide specialized surgical interventions
options.D: To provide daytime supervised care and support services

explanation: Adult day care homes are specifically designed to offer structured programs, supervision, and support during daytime hours while allowing clients to return home at night. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h1)

question: How do adult day care homes primarily benefit family caregivers?

options.A: By taking over complete legal and financial responsibility for the client
options.B: By training family members to become licensed practical nurses
options.C: By permanently removing the need for any home-based care
options.D: By offering temporary respite to prevent physical and emotional burnout

explanation: These facilities give family caregivers a necessary break from constant responsibilities, helping them sustain their own health and continue working or managing personal tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which model of adult day care focuses primarily on meals, recreation, and socialization without intensive health services?

options.A: Surgical model
options.B: Social model
options.C: Acute care model
options.D: Medical model

explanation: The social model is centered around community interaction, leisure activities, and basic supervision rather than active medical treatments. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h2)

question: A client with advanced Alzheimer's disease who wanders needs a secure environment with specialized cognitive programs. Which facility type is most appropriate?

options.A: Standard social model center
options.B: Acute psychiatric ward
options.C: Outpatient physical therapy clinic
options.D: Specialized model adult day center

explanation: Specialized models cater to specific groups like dementia patients, providing the required secure environments and targeted cognitive stimulation. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is a common inclusion criterion for admission to an adult day care home?

options.A: Mild to moderate functional decline requiring daytime supervision
options.B: Requirement for round-the-clock intensive surgical nursing
options.C: Comatose state requiring mechanical ventilation
options.D: Active and untreated infectious respiratory disease

explanation: Clients who need structured daytime support, socialization, or supervision while remaining at home at night are prime candidates for day care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which condition would most likely lead to a client being denied admission to a standard adult day care center?

options.A: Using a walker or cane for safe indoor mobility
options.B: Needing assistance with eating meals during the day
options.C: Mild forgetfulness associated with early-stage aging
options.D: Severe, unpredictable physical aggression toward others

explanation: Uncontrolled aggressive behaviors pose safety risks to staff and other participants, making standard day care settings unsuitable unless specialized behavioral resources exist. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of conducting regular nursing assessments in an adult day care setting?

options.A: To establish health baselines and catch subtle changes early
options.B: To enforce strict institutional rules upon the clients
options.C: To diagnose complex mental health disorders independently
options.D: To permanently replace the client's primary care physician

explanation: Regular assessments help nurses monitor chronic conditions and identify early signs of physical or cognitive deterioration before they become acute emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why does a comprehensive assessment in day care include evaluating the family caregiver?

options.A: To legally transfer family financial assets to the facility
options.B: To determine if the caregiver has a valid nursing license
options.C: To replace family involvement entirely with facility staff
options.D: To gauge caregiver stress and the sustainability of home care

explanation: Understanding caregiver strain helps the nursing team provide proper support and respite services, ensuring the client can safely remain at home. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h4)

question: How should therapeutic activities in adult day care be viewed?

options.A: As optional events that have no real health benefits
options.B: As purposeful interventions to enhance physical and cognitive well-being
options.C: As mandatory physical punishment for uncooperative behavior
options.D: As simple distractions to keep clients quiet until closing time

explanation: Activities are carefully chosen therapeutic tools designed to maintain mobility, stimulate memory, and promote social connection. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h5)

question: An activity coordinator plans a group exercise session. Which client adaptation best demonstrates person-centered care?

options.A: Excusing clients from participating if they look tired once
options.B: Requiring all clients to stand and follow the exact same routine
options.C: Skipping physical exercise altogether for safety reasons
options.D: Providing seated chair exercises for clients with poor balance

explanation: Adapting activities to individual functional levels, such as offering seated options, ensures safe and inclusive participation for everyone. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding medication management in adult day care?

options.A: Prescribing new medications whenever a client reports mild discomfort
options.B: Manufacturing custom pharmaceutical compounds on-site for each client
options.C: Allowing clients to share their prescription drugs freely among peers
options.D: Verifying orders, administering or supervising intake, and monitoring for side effects

explanation: Nurses ensure medication safety by checking dosages, administering or supervising consumption, and watching closely for adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why is routine health monitoring, such as checking blood glucose and blood pressure, essential in day care?

options.A: To detect early signs of chronic disease instability and prevent complications
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement without any practical clinical value
options.C: To punish clients who fail to follow their prescribed home diets
options.D: To diagnose acute surgical emergencies requiring immediate theater use

explanation: Regular monitoring catches small physiological shifts before they develop into dangerous health crises requiring hospitalization. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which group of professionals typically forms the core interprofessional team in an adult day care center?

options.A: Hospital administrators, accountants, and legal counsels
options.B: Nurses, social workers, activity coordinators, and therapists
options.C: Pharmacists, laboratory scientists, and radiologists
options.D: Surgeons, anesthetists, and operating room technicians

explanation: A multidisciplinary team combining nursing, social work, therapy, and recreation is standard for addressing holistic client needs. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h7)

question: How does close communication between nurses and family caregivers impact client care?

options.A: It ensures consistency between care practices at the center and at home
options.B: It prevents the nursing staff from making independent clinical choices
options.C: It creates unnecessary confusion and conflicting daily schedules
options.D: It allows the family to completely delegate all thinking to the staff

explanation: Sharing observations and strategies between home and the facility creates a unified approach that benefits the client's stability and comfort. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which safety measure is especially crucial in adult day care centers serving clients with cognitive impairment or dementia?

options.A: Restricted visiting hours for family members only
options.B: Locked individual client bedrooms for overnight sleeping
options.C: Mandatory physical restraints for all mobile participants
options.D: Secure entry and exit points to prevent wandering

explanation: Because many participants experience confusion or memory loss, controlled exits are vital to prevent elopement and ensure client safety. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting regular quality assurance audits in a day care facility?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any daily nursing supervision
options.B: To identify areas for improvement and maintain high standards of client safety
options.C: To increase daily attendance fees for participating families
options.D: To find staff members to blame when minor mistakes occur

explanation: Quality assurance reviews examine incident logs and procedures systematically to improve safety, prevent errors, and ensure regulatory compliance. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a subacute care facility?

options.A: Treating minor outpatient ailments and routine infections
options.B: Managing acute life-threatening surgical emergencies
options.C: Providing short-term rehabilitation and medical management
options.D: Offering permanent residential care for healthy elders

explanation: Spot on! Subacute care bridges the gap between the busy hospital ward and home, giving patients targeted rehab and recovery support. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which patient is the best fit for a subacute care unit?

options.A: A patient needing stable, step-down recovery after major surgery
options.B: A client needing long-term palliative care for terminal illness
options.C: An independent adult visiting a clinic for a routine checkup
options.D: A person requiring emergency trauma resuscitation in an ICU

explanation: You got it! These units are perfect for patients who are past the emergency phase but still need skilled nursing and therapy before heading home. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which condition often brings a patient to a subacute care unit?

options.A: Active cardiac arrest requiring immediate chest compressions
options.B: Routine annual physical examination and blood tests
options.C: Undiagnosed chronic fatigue without any physical findings
options.D: Recovery following a total knee replacement surgery

explanation: Correct! Post-surgical recovery that needs intensive physical therapy is a classic reason for subacute admission. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h2)

question: A stable patient needs daily IV antibiotics and physical therapy after a severe foot ulcer infection. Where should they be admitted?

options.A: An intensive care unit
options.B: A subacute care facility
options.C: An outpatient primary clinic
options.D: A long-term custodial home

explanation: Exactly! Needing daily skilled nursing (like IV medications) plus active therapy fits the exact description of subacute care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which specialist helps patients regain the ability to swallow safely?

options.A: Speech-language pathology
options.B: Occupational therapy
options.C: Respiratory therapy
options.D: Physical therapy

explanation: Spot on. Speech therapists evaluate and treat swallowing issues (dysphagia) to keep patients safe from choking or aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the main focus of occupational therapy in subacute care?

options.A: Helping patients perform daily self-care tasks like dressing and bathing
options.B: Managing complex intravenous medications and wound dressings
options.C: Assessing nutritional intake and feeding tube placement needs
options.D: Restoring walking ability and lower body muscle strength

explanation: You nailed it! Occupational therapy focuses on helping clients get back to doing everyday activities independently. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h3)

question: Why is sharp clinical assessment so important for nurses in subacute care?

options.A: Medical doctors are present on the unit twenty-four hours a day
options.B: Nurses perform emergency surgical procedures independently every day
options.C: Patients have complex chronic illnesses that can experience subtle signs of decline
options.D: Patients require continuous one-on-one monitoring identical to an ICU

explanation: Correct! Even during recovery, patients can experience quiet changes in their condition. Subacute nurses need sharp eyes to catch these early. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is a common myth about nursing work in subacute facilities?

options.A: It is merely custodial and does not require strong clinical assessment skills
options.B: It involves managing high-tech life support equipment in trauma bays
options.C: It focuses solely on discharging patients within twelve hours of arrival
options.D: It requires zero collaboration with physical or occupational therapists

explanation: Spot on. Some people wrongly think subacute care is just basic babysitting, missing the real clinical skills and monitoring required. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h4)

question: How does daily teamwork among different healthcare pros help a subacute patient?

options.A: It allows the team to adjust recovery goals based on shared observations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any written nursing documentation
options.C: It speeds up hospital discharge by removing the need for therapy
options.D: It ensures that doctors make all clinical decisions without staff input

explanation: You got it! Sharing updates across professions means the care plan matches the patient's daily energy and progress. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h5)

question: Who on the subacute care team is usually responsible for assessing nutritional needs?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Speech pathologist
options.D: Registered dietitian

explanation: Correct! Dietitians check nutritional status and plan the right meals or tube-feeding formulas to speed up healing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h5)

question: When should discharge planning ideally start for a patient in subacute care?

options.A: After physical therapy finishes
options.B: Forty-eight hours before leaving
options.C: When the family requests it
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Spot on! Starting on day one ensures home changes, equipment, and family training are sorted out without last-minute rush. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is teaching family caregivers a key part of subacute discharge planning?

options.A: It allows family members to legally substitute for trained nurses
options.B: It removes the need for any follow-up visits with primary doctors
options.C: It ensures the facility receives additional government funding
options.D: It prepares them to safely manage medications and care tasks at home

explanation: You nailed it. Equipping family caregivers prevents slip-ups and keeps the patient from bouncing back to the hospital. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard clinical quality indicator tracked in subacute facilities?

options.A: Development of new facility-acquired pressure injuries
options.B: Unplanned acute hospital readmission rates
options.C: Daily visitor parking satisfaction scores
options.D: Incidence of preventable medication administration errors

explanation: Correct! Parking is nice, but patient safety metrics like pressure sores, infections, and readmissions are what truly matter clinically. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h7)

question: What is the main reason for monitoring quality indicators in subacute care?

options.A: To punish staff members who make minor documentation errors
options.B: To identify gaps in care and protect patient safety
options.C: To justify reducing the number of licensed nurses on duty
options.D: To increase the speed of patient turnover at any cost

explanation: Spot on! Tracking quality data helps the team spot system flaws early and keep patient care safe and top-notch. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h7)

question: What is the main difference between an acute care hospital and a long-term care (LTC) facility?

options.A: Hospitals focus solely on long-term chronic illnesses
options.B: LTC facilities serve as a long-term home focused on support
options.C: Hospitals provide more rehabilitation and personal care
options.D: LTC facilities only admit patients for short-term surgeries

explanation: You've got this! While hospitals are for short, emergency or curative visits, LTC facilities are designed to be a supportive home where residents live and receive ongoing care for extended periods. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which setting is best for an older adult who needs round-the-clock nursing checks and complex wound care?

options.A: Assisted living facility
options.B: Skilled nursing facility
options.C: Independent living apartment
options.D: Continuing care retirement community

explanation: Great thinking! A skilled nursing facility provides the 24/7 professional nursing oversight needed for heavy clinical tasks like complex wound care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is the nurse-resident relationship in long-term care so special compared to acute care?

options.A: Family members take over all nursing responsibilities
options.B: Extended stay allows for deeper therapeutic relationships
options.C: Short patient stays prevent any meaningful connections
options.D: Nurses only interact with residents during medication passes

explanation: Spot on! Because residents live there for months or years, you really get to know them and their families, which helps you notice even the smallest changes in their health. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h2)

question: An LTC nurse spends a big part of the shift supervising nursing assistants. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To minimize direct nurse interaction with residents
options.B: To ensure delegated tasks are performed safely and correctly
options.C: To complete administrative paperwork required by the hospital
options.D: To replace the need for formal care planning meetings

explanation: You got it! As the professional nurse, you lead the care team and oversee assistants to make sure daily tasks like hygiene and safety are done properly. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of assessment tools like the Minimum Data Set (MDS) in long-term care?

options.A: To systematically evaluate resident health status and functional capacity
options.B: To replace the need for daily nursing vital sign documentation
options.C: To bill insurance companies for emergency room visits
options.D: To determine the discharge date for acute hospital recovery

explanation: Well done! Tools like the MDS give us a clear, organized way to track how a resident's physical and mental abilities change over time. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h3)

question: A nurse notices a resident's food intake has dropped sharply over two weeks. What is the best next step?

options.A: Collaborate with the interprofessional team to update the care plan
options.B: Wait for the annual assessment to record the weight loss
options.C: Discharge the resident to an assisted living facility
options.D: Stop monitoring meal intake since preferences change

explanation: Exactly right! Care plans are living documents. When a change happens, we team up with dietitians and doctors right away to update the plan and help the resident. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic geriatric syndrome often managed in long-term care?

options.A: Acute appendicitis
options.B: Bacterial meningitis
options.C: Pressure injuries
options.D: Compound fractures

explanation: Keep shining! Pressure injuries, falls, and confusion are common multi-factorial challenges we look out for in frail older adults. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why is sudden delirium in an older adult in long-term care such an urgent concern?

options.A: It has no impact on the resident's daily functional abilities
options.B: It only occurs immediately following surgical procedures
options.C: It represents an acute change in cognition often signaling an underlying infection
options.D: It is a normal, permanent part of the normal aging process

explanation: Spot on! Delirium is never 'just old age'—it's an emergency sign that something else, like a urinary tract infection, is wrong in the body. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the core focus of person-centered care in a long-term care facility?

options.A: Honoring the individual resident's preferences and autonomy
options.B: Prioritizing staff convenience over resident daily routines
options.C: Enforcing a strict schedule for all residents to follow
options.D: Treating all residents with identical medical protocols

explanation: Wonderful! Person-centered care means respecting the unique choices, life history, and dignity of every single resident instead of a one-size-fits-all rule. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h5)

question: How does promoting social activities and engagement directly help long-term care residents?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for chronic disease medications
options.B: It shortens the required recovery time from acute infections
options.C: It helps combat depression and feelings of loneliness
options.D: It replaces physical therapy interventions for mobility

explanation: You nailed it! Isolation is tough in facilities; meaningful activities give residents joy, purpose, and a big boost to their mental well-being. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why are congregate living settings like nursing homes particularly vulnerable to disease outbreaks?

options.A: The complete absence of handwashing sinks
options.B: The high rate of sudden resident discharges
options.C: The requirement for outdoor recreational sports
options.D: The close proximity of medically frail residents

explanation: Correct! When vulnerable people live close together, germs can spread fast unless we are super strict with our infection control. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a main focus during external regulatory inspections of a nursing home?

options.A: Checking employee vacation requests and holiday schedules
options.B: Evaluating medication administration accuracy and safety
options.C: Ensuring residents' rights and personal dignity are protected
options.D: Assessing environmental safety and infection control practices

explanation: You got this! Inspectors care about resident safety, care quality, and rights—they don't mind who takes holiday when! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in a long-term care setting?

options.A: Curing the underlying chronic terminal disease
options.B: Eliminating the need for family involvement
options.C: Accelerating the physical dying process safely
options.D: Relieving pain and managing distressing symptoms

explanation: Wonderful job! Palliative care is all about maximizing comfort, easing heavy symptoms, and bringing peace of mind to patients with serious illnesses. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why should nurses discuss advance directives and goals of care early with residents and their families?

options.A: To ensure the resident's personal wishes are honored when a crisis occurs
options.B: To remove the physician from making any future medical decisions
options.C: To shorten the length of stay in the long-term care facility
options.D: To eliminate the need for family communication at the end of life

explanation: Spot on! Talking about wishes early ensures that if a crisis hits and the resident can't speak, we still honor what they truly wanted. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is a main goal of managing nutrition issues during home care visits?

options.A: Reducing daily fluid intake
options.B: Eliminating family involvement
options.C: Preventing severe malnutrition and hospital readmissions
options.D: Ensuring only imported foods are eaten

explanation: Early identification and management of feeding hurdles stop nutritional decline before it requires acute hospital admission. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why must nurses look beyond just the food on the plate during home visits?

options.A: Physical, mental, and social barriers often cause feeding issues
options.B: Food presentation is the only factor for appetite
options.C: Patients rarely eat what relatives prepare
options.D: Hospital food standards must be used everywhere

explanation: Nutritional intake is affected by many factors including hand dexterity, memory loss, and cultural beliefs, not just food availability. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h1)

question: Muscle wasting and slow wound healing are classic signs of which condition?

options.A: Protein-Energy Malnutrition
options.B: Iron-Deficiency Anemia
options.C: Acute dehydration
options.D: Fluid overload

explanation: A shortage of both calories and protein robs the body of building blocks needed for tissue repair and maintenance. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the main issue for a patient diagnosed with dysphagia?

options.A: A psychological refusal to eat
options.B: Painful swelling of the salivary glands
options.C: Craving non-food items like clay or ice
options.D: Difficulty moving food safely from the mouth to the stomach

explanation: Dysphagia refers strictly to swallowing impairments that affect the passage of solids or liquids down the esophagus. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h2)

question: Which neurological condition directly impairs the muscle control needed for safe swallowing?

options.A: Stroke
options.B: Essential tremor
options.C: Chronic tension headache
options.D: Peripheral neuropathy

explanation: Cerebrovascular accidents often damage brain centers responsible for coordinating the complex swallowing mechanism. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h3)

question: How do money constraints contribute to nutrition problems in home care patients?

options.A: They prevent the digestive tract from absorbing vitamins
options.B: They increase the body's need for calories
options.C: They cause immediate neurological damage
options.D: They limit the patient's ability to buy and prepare nourishing food

explanation: Poverty restricts access to a diverse, protein-rich diet, which directly drives nutritional deficiencies at home. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h3)

question: What is a practical alternative measurement when a weighing scale is missing during a home visit?

options.A: Mid-upper arm circumference
options.B: Chest wall expansion
options.C: Abdominal skinfold depth
options.D: Head circumference

explanation: Measuring the upper arm provides a reliable proxy for muscle mass and nutritional status when weighing scales are unavailable. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h4)

question: Why are standardized screening tools used during early home care visits?

options.A: To determine family income
options.B: To replace physical exams and lab tests
options.C: To calculate exact daily water requirements
options.D: To identify patients at nutritional risk before severe decline happens

explanation: Screening tools catch subtle signs of impending malnutrition early, allowing prompt dietary intervention. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary danger of food entering the airway below the vocal cords?

options.A: Aspiration pneumonia
options.B: Chronic hypertension
options.C: Permanent vocal cord paralysis
options.D: Severe gastric ulcer

explanation: Foreign material in the lower respiratory tract introduces bacteria and causes dangerous lung infections. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why should a patient remain upright for thirty minutes after finishing a meal?

options.A: It prevents sudden abdominal cramps
options.B: It lets tongue muscles rest
options.C: Gravity helps keep food down and stops it from entering the airway
options.D: It speeds up stomach emptying

explanation: Remaining upright uses gravity to keep stomach contents from refluxing into the pharynx and risking aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h5)

question: What minimum head-of-bed elevation is needed during tube feeding to prevent reflux?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees upright
options.C: 60 to 75 degrees
options.D: Zero degrees flat

explanation: Elevating the head of the bed uses gravity to reduce the risk of formula flowing back up into the esophagus and airway. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h6)

question: Why is regular flushing of a feeding tube necessary?

options.A: To prevent formula from clogging the narrow tube
options.B: To stimulate bowel movements
options.C: To replace IV hydration therapy
options.D: To cool down the liquid formula

explanation: Flushing water through the tube before and after feeds clears leftover formula and stops the tube from blocking. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h6)

question: Why are small, frequent meals recommended for patients with poor appetite?

options.A: They eliminate the need for protein
options.B: They feel less overwhelming than large plates of food
options.C: They cure swallowing disorders
options.D: They reduce daily calorie intake

explanation: Large portions often discourage weak or anorexic patients, whereas small amounts are easier to manage. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h7)

question: How does ensuring proper denture fit improve a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It prevents food from entering the nose
options.B: It increases digestive enzymes in saliva
options.C: It speeds up food movement in the esophagus
options.D: It eliminates mouth pain and makes chewing comfortable

explanation: Ill-fitting dentures cause gum sores and pain, which directly causes patients to reject solid foods. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h7)

question: What is a key warning sign that caregivers must report during feeding?

options.A: Sleeping after lunchtime
options.B: Coughing during meals
options.C: Wearing clean clothing
options.D: Drinking water quietly

explanation: Coughing while eating or drinking suggests that food or liquid is penetrating the airway, indicating aspiration risk. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h8)

question: Why must nurses tailor diet advice to local food availability and money?

options.A: Local foods lack nutrients
options.B: Imported foods cause allergies
options.C: Caregivers refuse cooking advice
options.D: Unrealistic diet plans are impossible for families to maintain

explanation: If recommended foods are too expensive or unavailable locally, the care plan will inevitably fail at home. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h8)

question: Which specialist should a nurse consult if a patient shows worsening swallowing difficulties?

options.A: Laboratory technician
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Speech therapist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Speech therapists specialize in evaluating and treating swallowing disorders and performing bedside swallow evaluations. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h9)

question: Why is accurate record-keeping of daily food intake important?

options.A: It replaces weighing the patient
options.B: It calculates meal costs
options.C: It proves the family bought expensive food
options.D: It provides a clear record for the healthcare team

explanation: Tracking exact intake trends allows dietitians and doctors to modify nutritional prescriptions safely. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h9)

question: What does a patient who needs verbal cues during grooming require?

options.A: Minimal assistance
options.B: Total dependence
options.C: Maximal assistance
options.D: Supervision

explanation: Supervision involves overseeing the task and providing verbal prompts rather than physical lifting. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why should nurses assess a patient's baseline ability before assisting with personal care?

options.A: To reduce the time spent writing nursing care plans
options.B: To eliminate the need for family caregiver education
options.C: To prevent the loss of remaining functional skills
options.D: To determine the hospital discharge date immediately

explanation: Allowing patients to perform tasks they are still capable of doing preserves their strength and independence. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which part of the body should be washed first during a bed bath?
